title: Is the cost of education less than one-fourth the cost of food?
description: The education and food bars of a family's spending graph are compared using one-fourth. Dividing the food amount by four and checking the bars side by side give the same answer, and Keeko's doubt, that a number close to one-fourth counts as one-fourth, is checked.
teaching_notes: One idea: find one-fourth by dividing by four, then compare, because close is not the same. Watch for students who round and say the two are equal.

source: Is the cost of education less than one-fourth the cost of food? (Education 800, Food 3400.)
video_script.why: The child finds one-fourth of a larger amount by dividing by four and compares it with a smaller amount, then checks on the bars.
video_script.substitution: Divide the cost of food by four, compare the result with the cost of education, and check by putting four education bars beside the food bar.
video_script.anchor: the bar graph of the monthly spending of the family, with the education bar of 4 units and the food bar of 17 units
video_script.wrong_answer: no, because eight hundred is close to eight hundred and fifty
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko treats a number close to one-fourth as one-fourth. Eight hundred is smaller than eight hundred and fifty, even if only by a little.
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, the cost of education is less than one-fourth of the cost of food

final_answer.value: Yes. One-fourth of 3400 is 850 and 800 is less than 850
final_answer.spoken: yes, the cost of education is less than one-fourth of the cost of food, because eight hundred is less than eight hundred and fifty

hold_back: less than one-fourth of the cost of food
maths_rules: food 3400 rupees = 17 units, education 800 rupees = 4 units, scale 1 unit = Rs 200
check on the graph: 4 x 4 = 16 units, which is less than 17 units
video_script.design: One idea: one-fourth is food divided by four, and then we compare. The graph stays on the board all video and four copies of the education bar are stacked beside the food bar.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the same family spending graph.
<bookmark mark='graph'/>Look at the bar for education and the bar for food.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Is the cost of education less than one fourth the cost of food?

beats.on_screen: the graph stays on the board and Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a bar of 12 squares split into four equal bars of 3 squares; the words one of four equal parts, one fourth appear

marks.twelve: a bar of twelve squares appears
marks.split: it splits into four equal bars of three squares each
marks.word: the words one of four equal parts, one fourth appear

narration: <bookmark mark='twelve'/>Take a bar that is twelve squares tall.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Split it into four equal parts, and each part is three squares tall.
<bookmark mark='word'/>One of the four equal parts is called one fourth. We find it by dividing by four.

beats.on_screen: Given: Education 800 rupees, 4 units; Food 3400 rupees, 17 units
narration: <bookmark mark='edu'/>Given, education costs eight hundred rupees, which is a bar of four units.
<bookmark mark='food'/>Food costs three thousand four hundred rupees, which is a bar of seventeen units.

beats.on_screen: To find: is the cost of education less than one-fourth the cost of food?
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to compare education with one fourth of food.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, find one fourth of the food cost. Split three thousand four hundred into three thousand and four hundred.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Three thousand divided by four is seven hundred and fifty.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Four hundred divided by four is one hundred.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Seven hundred and fifty plus one hundred is eight hundred and fifty.

marks.two: 800 and 850 are written side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, compare education with one fourth of food. Education is eight hundred, and one fourth of food is eight hundred and fifty.
<bookmark mark='less'/>Eight hundred is less than eight hundred and fifty.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: check on the graph. 4 copies of the education bar stack to 4 x 4 = 16 units, one unit short of the 17 units of the food bar

marks.copy: four copies of the education bar are stacked beside the food bar
marks.short: the stack reaches 16 units and stops one unit below the food bar

narration: <bookmark mark='copy'/>Step three, check on the graph. Stack four copies of the education bar beside the food bar.
<bookmark mark='short'/>The stack stops a little below the food bar.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Four times four is sixteen units, and the food bar is seventeen.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Yes. One-fourth of 3400 is 850 and 800 is less than 850
narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Yes, the cost of education is less than one-fourth of the cost of food.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the bar graph
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble says no, because 800 is close to 850; the bubble is struck through; the 16-unit stack and the 17-unit food bar are shown with the gap of one unit

marks.gap: the gap of one unit between the stack and the food bar is shaded
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the gap stays shaded

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is no, because eight hundred is close to eight hundred and fifty.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>But close is not the same. The question asks if it is less, and a small gap still counts.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The shaded gap on the graph shows that the stack really is shorter.
